title: Cabled fingerless mitts in DK wool
subtitle: Six-stitch cable panel on the back of the hand, with afterthought thumb.
excerpt: Fingerless mitts with a six-stitch cable running up the back of the hand on a 1×1 rib background. Worked in the round in DK wool. Afterthought thumb. Sized for 18, 20, and 22 cm hand circumferences.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 14th series (1880s), §Cabled mittens. Cable-panel mittens and mitts appear in Weldon's and in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Mittens and gloves with decorative panels. Both are out of UK and EU copyright.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rounds = 10 × 10 cm in 1×1 rib slightly stretched on 3.75 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning to them after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A short auxiliary needle used to hold stitches to the front or back while a cable crossing is worked. The held stitches are then knitted in the new order to form the cross.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Fingerless mitts with a six-stitch cable panel running up the back of the hand, on a 1×1 rib background, sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
The construction is seamless, worked in the round using
magic loop
on a long circular. The cable is a six-stitch back cross worked every 8th round. On the palm side the fabric is 1×1 rib throughout. The thumb uses the
afterthought thumb
method. Budget about 90 g (200 m / 220 yards) of DK wool. The cable uses a
cable needle
to hold 3 stitches to the back while the next 3 are knitted, then the held stitches are knitted.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 90 g (about 200 m / 220 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Cable needle
items.qty: 1 — a short straight or J-shaped cable needle

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 3 — 1 for the beginning of the round, 2 to flank the cable panel

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the afterthought thumb

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 30 rounds to 10 cm over 1×1 rib slightly stretched on 3.75 mm needles. The cable panel pulls in more tightly than the rib. The finished width is set by the rib gauge, not the cable gauge.
Cable chart

items.name: Round 8 (cross round)
items.qty: Slip 3 stitches to cable needle and hold at back. k3. k3 from cable needle.

content.text: Stitches used

items.name: C6B
items.qty: cable 6 back: slip 3 to cable needle and hold back, k3, k3 from cable needle

content.text: Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count and measurement reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 36 (40, 44) stitches. All sizes are even numbers so 1×1 rib joins cleanly. Join to work in the round, placing the beginning-of-round marker. Work 1×1 rib (k1, p1 every round) for 20 (22, 24) rounds.
Set up the cable

The cable sits on the back of the hand, centred over the knuckles. The beginning of the round is at the palm side. Work across 15 (17, 19) palm stitches in 1×1 rib, PM (first cable marker), k6 (the cable panel), PM (second cable marker), continue in 1×1 rib to end.
Hand and thumb position
Work 8 (10, 10) rounds: work palm in 1×1 rib, SM, k6 (or C6B on round 8), SM, continue in rib.

Thumb marker round: work 8 (9, 10) palm stitches in rib, then knit the next 8 (9, 10) stitches with waste yarn, slip them back and knit with main yarn, continue in pattern to end. The waste yarn marks the thumb opening on the palm side.
Hand above thumb
Continue working the cable panel and rib for a further 16 (18, 20) rounds, working C6B on rounds 8 and 16. Bind off in 1×1 rib.
Thumb

Remove waste yarn from the thumb gap, picking up 8 (9, 10) live stitches above and 8 (9, 10) live stitches below. Total: 16 (18, 20) thumb stitches. Work 10 (12, 12) rounds of 1×1 rib. Bind off in rib.
Common faults

Cable twists the wrong direction: the cross round slipped stitches to the front instead of the back. C6B always holds stitches at the back. A front-cross gives a left-leaning cable instead of a right-leaning one.
Cable panel is off-centre: the marker placement on the set-up round was not centred. Count the palm stitches before and after the cable markers; they should match for each size.

Cable too tight to work: you are working into the stitches at the back of the cable needle with the working needle tip rather than knitting them freely. Hold the cable needle parallel to the left needle and knit the stitches off it as normal.
Finishing
Weave in all yarn tails on the wrong side. Close any small holes at the thumb corners.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with a wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry. Blocking the cable panel on a padded surface gives a crisper result.
What to try next
Two cable columns on either side of a centre purl column, worked on a full mitten body, is the next step from this single-cable mitt.
